audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup states twice that Wind Wall 'can only block one projectile per cast' and calls it a 'single-target Windwall'. That is false and it is the single most decisive interaction in the lane.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds', 400 range, 25/23/21/19/17s. Kennen's Q is flagged projectile and is blocked outright; Electrical Surge (W), Lightning Rush (E) and Slicing Maelstrom (R) are not projectiles and pass through it, which is why the stun chain still works into a held wall.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall blocks every projectile for 4 seconds on a 25s rank-1 cooldown — hold Q, and stack marks with W/E/R, which it cannot stop.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five level rows disagree with the packet chart and with the matchup's own why text: Level 1 is Kennen although whys[0] says it reads even; Level 2 is 'Skill', Levels 3 and 4-5 are Yasuo and First item is Yasuo, although whys[1] through whys[5] all describe Kennen winning those stages outright.
audit.why: Yasuo has no sustain and a 25s Wind Wall at rank 1, so Kennen's mark chip is uncontested between casts. The 55.85% Emerald+ win rate over 573 games agrees. Only the 2+ item row belongs to Yasuo.
audit.corrected: Level 1 = Skill, Level 2 = Kennen, Level 3 = Kennen, Levels 4-5 = Kennen, First item = Kennen; Level 6 stays Kennen and 2+ items stays Yasuo.

audit.why: Kennen at 2-3, level 6 Slicing Maelstrom (120s) and first item are right, and Yasuo's takeover at Shieldbow plus crit is right. Note his Last Breath is 70/50/30s, so it is up far more often late than Kennen's 120s R.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — you both have fragile bodies, and his Windwall (W) eats your Q the second you telegraph it, so don't waste your only poke into a held wall. Last-hit at max Q range and fire it when he's mid-E-dash or his Windwall is on cooldown. From Level 2-3 your Electrical Surge (W) on-hit autos plus a second Q point let you stack Mark of the Storm faster than one Windwall can block, and he has no sustain to heal the chip — he can only block one projectile per cast, so bait the wall, then re-Q.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you both have fragile bodies, and Wind Wall eats your Q the second you telegraph it, so don't waste your only poke into a held wall. Last-hit at max Q range and fire it when he is mid-Sweeping Blade or the wall is on its 25-second cooldown. From Level 2-3 your Electrical Surge on-hit autos and Lightning Rush stack Mark of the Storm with no projectile for the wall to block, and he has no sustain to heal the chip — so bait the wall, then re-Q.

notes: Killed a false mechanic repeated across three fields: Wind Wall was written as blocking 'one projectile per cast'. Riot's text is 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds'. The useful true fact is the opposite framing — Kennen's W, E and R are not projectiles and go through it, which is why the stun chain still lands. Level chart rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 flipped as one atomic group across both layers. Separately: diff is TRICKY at 7.5/10 while the win rate is 55.85% and Kennen now owns every row through first item — the user may want that difficulty re-rated, but I left it since difficulty can legitimately mean execution difficulty.
